walkthroughs.body_html: pH is the negative log10 of H+ ion concentration. A change from pH 8.2 to 7.2 represents 10 times more H+. Pre-industrial 8.2 to today's 8.1 represents roughly 26 percent more H+. By 2100 under high-emissions scenarios pH could fall to about 7.8, more than 100 percent higher H+ vs pre-industrial.

Aragonite saturation state (omega) above 1 means seawater is supersaturated and shells form easily. Below 1 they dissolve. Cold waters near the poles already approach omega = 1, threatening pteropods that form the base of many polar food webs. Tropical reefs need omega above 3 to thrive.

Under high-emissions RCP 8.5, surface ocean pH could fall to about 7.8 by 2100, leaving most coral reefs below survival thresholds. Under low-emission RCP 2.6, pH stays nearer 8.05, giving reefs a fighting chance if combined with reduced local pollution and overfishing. Mitigation choices today shape ocean futures.
